state: An editor session synchronously calls an analysis backend with a borrowed shared source database and current source ID. IDs denote immutable bytes only within their database owner; callers cannot hold the borrowed session database through a mutation. The session currently accumulates distinct revisions. Its callbacks can see all open documents, although supported analysis selects one file. Queued publication checks URI/version/source identity and close cancels document jobs. Separate public compilation owners are immutable append-only and may be retained; checked programs authenticate their original owner and ordered file selection. A moderate edit probe confirms retained text growth, and the lint driver visits old files outside the checked selection. The repair must bound session-owned obsolete data, restrict lint to checked files, preserve public held owners and callback signatures, and preserve pending publication and reopen behavior without expanding project analysis.

ownership.instructions: For these verified abstract semantics, which ownership alternative is most suitable overall? Balance compatibility, task identity, resource behavior and long-term maintenance; do not privilege a smaller incomplete patch.

criteria.live_owner: Fresh session-only storage after distinct changes and close contains exactly live texts. Deterministically remap document IDs and all still-current queued jobs; cancel stale jobs before numeric ID aliasing. External immutable databases are untouched. Trades zero retained history and narrow production scope against repeated live-document cloning/hashing.
criteria.reclamation_api: Build an immutable snapshot storage abstraction with generational IDs and retained leases. Migrate live documents/queued jobs and compatibility callers; reclaim only snapshots whose leases have ended, preserving public legacy owners and checked provenance. Trades reduced live-set copying against new API complexity and larger compatibility closure.
criteria.bounded_history: Keep append-only obsolete session texts until a specified revision ceiling, then rebuild from live texts and remap valid work. Preserve external owners. Trades fewer rebuilds against threshold policy, bounded but unnecessary retained data, and counter/remapping maintenance.
